assumptions.status: Hypothetical iris assumptions; the colorimetry tables and the measured Sarna & Swartz 1988 melanin spectral shapes are sourced; the 550 nm magnitudes and everything else remain assumptions

colorimetry.colour_space: CIE 1976 L*a*b*; white is a perfect reflector under the same sampled tables

assumptions.eumelanin_spectral_exponent_provenance: SUPERSEDED — retained for provenance only, UNUSED in this run. The spectral shape is now the measured Sarna & Swartz 1988 data (see melanin_spectra). Previously: Jacques OMLC https://omlc.org/spectra/melanin/mua.html (retrieved 2026-10-26).
assumptions.pheomelanin_spectral_exponent_provenance: SUPERSEDED — retained for provenance only, UNUSED in this run. The spectral shape is now the measured Sarna & Swartz 1988 data (see melanin_spectra). Previously: assumed and swept; no visible-range pheomelanin spectrum had been found in open sources.

melanin_spectra.source: Sarna T., Swartz H.M., The physical properties of melanins, in The Pigmentary System, ed. J.J. Nordlund et al., Oxford University Press, 1988
melanin_spectra.host: Natural Phenomena Simulation Group, University of Waterloo / Oregon Medical Laser Center
melanin_spectra.normalization: Each spectrum is divided by its extinction at 550 nm so that the shape equals 1.0 at 550 nm. Eumelanin 550 = 5.79; pheomelanin 550 = 2.994 (units: decadic extinction coefficient, cm^-1 (mg/ml)^-1).
melanin_spectra.provenance_note: The spectral SHAPES are now measured, replacing the previously assumed power-law exponents, which are retained above only for provenance and are UNUSED in this run. The 550 nm absorbance MAGNITUDES remain assumptions because no iris-specific absorption calibration was found.

measured_anchors.source: van den Berg, IJspeert and de Waard 1991, Vision Research 31:1361-1367, PMID 1891824; abstract read, full text not
measured_anchors.claim: For a light-blue eye effective transmission of the iris was 1% for red and 0.2% for green light
measured_anchors.limits: Non-albino iris. Transmission through the whole iris, not a round-trip return. The abstract reports dark-brown eyes two orders of magnitude lower. No albinism value was found.

melanin_spectra.source: Sarna T., Swartz H.M., The physical properties of melanins, in The Pigmentary System, ed. J.J. Nordlund et al., Oxford University Press, 1988; tabulated extinction coefficients hosted by the Waterloo NPSG / Oregon Medical Laser Center at https://www.npsg.uwaterloo.ca/data/skin/ (retrieved 2026-11-09; per-file sha256 pinned above).
melanin_spectra.limits: Extinction coefficients of extracted melanins in solution, not iris melanosomes in situ. Only the 550-normalized shapes are used; the absolute magnitudes at 550 nm remain assumptions.

eumelanin_spectral_exponent.status: superseded, retained for provenance only; UNUSED in this run
eumelanin_spectral_exponent.source: Jacques, https://omlc.org/spectra/melanin/mua.html (page copyright 1998 Steven Jacques; retrieved 2026-10-26; page sha256 0189e5bfd62a258bace15270d5e65615c1a6ee7093583766b308d8b40cd96d56). The page gives mu_a = 1.70e12 nm^-3.48 cm^-1 for skin and 6.49e12 nm^-3.48 cm^-1 for retina melanosome interiors and says ten-fold variation is to be expected. Only the exponent was used. It cites Jacques and McAuliffe 1991 (PMID 1886936; abstract read, full text not) and Jacques et al. 1996.
eumelanin_spectral_exponent.limits: Skin and retinal melanosomes, not iris, and not pheomelanin. The absolute magnitude was not used.

pheomelanin_spectral_exponent.status: superseded, retained for provenance only; UNUSED in this run. Was assumed and swept because no visible-range measurement had been found in open sources.
pheomelanin_spectral_exponent.qualitative_support: Peles and Simon 2010 (PMID 20614877; abstract read) report pheomelanin absorption 1.2 times eumelanin at 244 nm and infer it is lower at 315-400 nm, so it may fall off faster. That is ultraviolet only.

stroma_backscatter.status: assumed and swept, then calibrated: only settings whose pigment-free stroma over a dark back falls in the blue window are used for interpretation
stroma_backscatter.note: No quantitative open source for iris stroma scattering amplitude or wavelength dependence was found. A Monte Carlo model of lightly pigmented irides exists (Baranoski and Lam 2007, DOI 10.1117/1.2747205); its title resolved and it was not read.

back_return_modes.status: assumed and swept; the red edge position and width are assumed; see measured_anchors for the only related measurement found

notes: Absorbance values are single-pass over the stroma at 550 nm for the combined melanins.
Melanin spectral shapes are the measured Sarna & Swartz 1988 extinction coefficients, linearly interpolated and normalized to 1.0 at 550 nm; the 550 nm magnitudes remain assumptions.
Backscatter is bounded (fraction at 550 nm times (550/lambda)^exponent, capped at 1).
The translucent_red_return modes stand in for a reddish return through a pigment-poor, translucent iris.
A case is classified only if its luminance Y is at least the stated fraction of the reference's, so very dark pigment-saturated cases are not counted as orange or purple.
Colour uses the CIE tables in cie-tables/, sampled at the model wavelengths. CIELAB hue angle does not change when a spectrum is uniformly dimmed, so brightness and hue are judged separately.
D65 is a reference daylight, not a viewing condition. Real appearance also depends on lighting, adaptation, surroundings and camera processing.
Windows are hue-angle ranges centred on reference spectra chosen for this exploration; they are not definitions of the words orange or purple.
A measured pheomelanin visible spectrum is no longer an outstanding input; a measured back return still is.
